notes.title: Operating philosophy
notes.body: This is a coaching first org. Leaders spend their time coaching: team meetings, 1:1s, reviewing calls and emails, and giving real time feedback. Managers and directors must have serious hands on MDR experience, know how to coach, and have been coached themselves. We deliberately avoid an org bogged down in tools training and low value meetings.

notes.title: Span of control
notes.body: One manager per 8 MDRs to leave real room for coaching. One director per roughly 50 MDRs. That lands at 30 managers and 5 directors. The org is seeded at 240 seats to drive 9k demos per quarter

notes.title: Messaging is owned by Product Marketing
notes.body: Product Marketing already provides messaging and content, so messaging and sequences is owned by PMM

notes.title: Enablement stays lean
notes.body:
Enablement is deliberately a single role that is setup to onboard the team the first 90 days, then hand to managers. 

If tools training, platforms are needed, existing enablement can help.

notes.title: Existing shared functions
notes.body: Operations (rev ops within Richards org), Sales Recruiter, and Content / Messaging already exist on the current team.

notes.title: Phase 1, hire the org to capacity
notes.body: Phase 1 is 106 net new hires: 80 internal MDRs plus the leadership to support them, 12 managers at one per 8, 2 directors, 1 MDR Trainer and the Head of SMB Sales. It runs alongside what already exists rather than replacing it.

notes.title: The overage is deliberate
notes.body: Capacity today is 181, which is 31 internal plus 150 outsourced. The 80 Phase 1 hires take working capacity to 271, roughly 30 over the 240 target. That buffer is on purpose. Hiring is constant and ongoing so we can weed out and replace underperformers without dropping below the number.

notes.title: Phase 2, replace outsourced and legacy with internal
notes.body: Phase 2 swaps the 150 outsourced MDRs for internal MDRs and rebuilds the 31 legacy internal seats with their 4 managers and 1 director into the end state structure. Leadership builds out to 30 managers and 5 directors. After continuous trimming the org settles at roughly 240 fully internal MDRs.

notes.title: Assumption on the legacy leaders
notes.body: The model absorbs the 4 existing managers and 1 existing director into the 30 and 5 end state, so Phase 2 adds 14 managers and 2 directors. If those leaders are replaced rather than kept, Phase 2 is 18 managers and 3 directors instead.

roleDefinitions.title: Head of SMB Sales
responsibilities: Owns the entire MDR org, its number of 9,000 completed demos per quarter, and the operating model.
Builds and leads the leadership layer, sets the coaching culture, and hires and develops the directors.
Owns the two phase build: Phase 1 hires to capacity, Phase 2 replaces the outsourced and legacy teams with internal MDRs.
Owns capacity planning, headcount ramp, targets, comp
Stays close to the floor and protects the org from meeting and tool bloat.

roleDefinitions.title: Director of MDR
responsibilities: Owns a segment of about 50 MDRs across roughly 6 managers, and their share of the demo target.
Develops and coaches the managers, the coach the coach work, runs manager 1:1s, and holds the coaching standard.
Runs their share of the phase plan, whether that is standing up net new Phase 1 teams or converting outsourced seats to internal in Phase 2.
Accountable for team demo output, ramp, and quality, and removes blockers.
Must have real MDR and people management experience.

roleDefinitions.title: MDR Manager / Team Lead
responsibilities: Owns a team of 8 MDRs and their demo number.
Spends the majority of time coaching: team meetings, weekly 1:1s, reviewing calls and emails, and real time feedback.
Hires, ramps, develops, and manages the performance of the team, and runs the pod cadence.
Must have serious hands on MDR experience, know how to coach, and have been coached.

roleDefinitions.title: MDR
responsibilities: Owns 13 scheduled and 10 completed demos per month against target accounts.
Runs outbound across calls, email, and social, books and holds qualified demos, and hands off cleanly to AEs.
Executes the plays and messaging, which come from Product Marketing and are operationalized by Enablement, and acts on coaching.
Keeps CRM and activity data clean.

roleDefinitions.title: MDR New Hire Trainer
responsibilities: Owns new hire onboarding and ramp certification across the first 30, 60 and 90 days, and is accountable for ramp to productivity time.

roleDefinitions.title: Operations (sales ops)
responsibilities: Reporting, tooling, data, and comp and quota mechanics.

roleDefinitions.title: Sales Recruiter
responsibilities: Fills the hiring pipeline at wave velocity.

roleDefinitions.title: Product Marketing
responsibilities: Owns messaging, positioning, and content.

orgChart.notes: Builds the organization. Reports to the CEO. Sets a coaching first standard for every leader in the org.
